question: Which Act abolished the powers so long enjoyed by the Board of Control?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Act of 1858**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Board of Control and Court of Directors was abolished by the Government of India act 1858.__
 
• This act ended the system of double government in India.
 
• A new office called the Secretary of State was created, which vested with complete authority and control over Indian administration.
 
• A 15-member Council of India was established by the Government of India Act 1858 to assist the Secretary of state for India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Provisions of the Government of India Act 1858:**

 
 
• East India Company was liquidated.
 
• Indian territories of the British were to be governed in the name of the British queen
 
• The secretary of state was the channel of communication between the government in Britain and the Indian administration.
 
• The representatives of the British government in India were the governor-general and the viceroy.
 
• This act abolished the dual government of the Pitt India Act.
 
• This act also ended the doctrine of Lapse.
